target_customer: Startups and mid size companies in Latin America and other regions that need corporate cards, cross border payments and expense management
problem: Companies in Latin America struggle to get corporate credit cards and pay international vendors, because local banks do not serve them well.
business_model: Interchange and cross border payment fees on corporate cards plus credit (Jeeves Pay) and spend management software
product_category: Fintech, corporate cards and cross border payments

founders.name: Dileep Thazhmon
previous_startups: PowerInbox (email ad server, Battery Ventures backed)
founders.background_notes: From the YC page and TechCrunch June 2021; the YC page also says he worked in venture capital.

founders.name: Sherwin Gandhi
founders.background_notes: Named a founder by TechCrunch (June and September 2021); not listed on the YC page. No background found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Card issuing, multi currency payments and underwriting across several countries required licensed partners and integrations, but used standard fintech infrastructure.

defensibility.rationale: Local issuing and credit relationships in several countries and data for underwriting took time to build; card and spend software itself was copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch (June 2021) said competitors in each region plug into third party providers; no incumbent copying found.

market_need_then: Most Latin American companies could not get a corporate credit card, and the company grew from private beta in October 2020 with a waitlist above 5,000 companies by June 2021 per TechCrunch.

branding.domain_note: Uses tryjeeves.com and later jeeves.com style pages; acquisition history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Service oriented, implied by butler connotation

branding.community_and_virality: Celebrity angels Kevin Durant and Andre Iguodala drew press in September 2021.

brand_strength.rationale: Branding search found no company specific brand coverage; the name evokes the P. G. Wodehouse butler and the Ask Jeeves search engine, which may confuse search. Celebrity backers added press.

outcome_analysis: Jeeves went from YC Summer 2020 to a 2.1 billion valuation by March 2022 with seed, Series A, B and C inside about 18 months, driven by unserved demand for corporate cards in Latin America and a strong investor group. It added Jeeves Pay and stablecoin payouts and raised debt in 2024. No exit or shutdown found, though later growth equity details were not verified.
notes: Competitors left empty: Clara and others appear in sources dated May 2021 or later, beyond a few months after the batch, and TechCrunch June 2021 names no rivals. Search summaries mention a later 110M round led by CoinFund and a 2026 raise, both seen in snippets only and not recorded; one aggregator lists 653M total, unverified. Series A: the 100M debt was reported alongside the 26M equity, and 5M seed was announced at the same time. Series C amounts and valuation stated by several outlets (PYMNTS, TechCrunch, Finance Magnates).
